# AGENTS.md — shapes

existing project · architecture: minimal · domain: general
Stack: Node.js · API: REST with DTO boundaries · Testing: npm test

This project uses spec-driven development with `specgate`. `spec.md`,
`features/` and `docs/specs/` are the contract your work is judged against.

## Work

1. `specgate status` — what is left, and the next requirement.
2. Write the test first and name the requirement in it (`REQ-007`, and its
   scenario `SCN-007a` when there is one). That mention is the link.
3. Implement until `specgate check` passes: specs, links, coverage, tests.
4. `specgate done REQ-007` — refused unless the gate passes.

Each step in detail: the `/specgate:*` commands, or
`specgate change instructions <artifact> --json`.

## From a plan or brief

`specgate draft` names the next module of `docs/brief.md`; `specgate draft
<module>` opens it and writes `DRAFTING.md` — follow it, then re-run until
"Ready to review". Never archive a draft yourself: a person reviews it.

## Never

- Edit `spec.md`, `features/`, `docs/specs/` or this file to make a test pass.
- Choose or replace the stack; if a field above is TBD, stop and ask.
- Say work is done that `specgate check` has not passed.

## Project rules

- The test command is `npm test`.
- Never delete or weaken an existing test to get to green.
- One requirement at a time: extend or write the test first, then the code.
- Do not modify generated or vendored code unless the requirement says so.
- Keep business logic out of framework code: no business rules in controllers, components, or infrastructure adapters.
